content: 1. Rose hips enhance the gastrointestinal (GI) absorption of calcium chloride, increasing its levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and currently unknown. 2. Calcium citrate reduces the levels of rose hips by inhibiting their GI absorption. Conversely, rose hips increase calcium citrate levels by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 3. Calcium gluconate decreases the levels of rose hips by inhibiting their GI absorption, while rose hips increase calcium gluconate levels by enhancing GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 4. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefamandole, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefditoren, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefotetan, cefoxitin, cefpirome, cefpodoxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, ceftriaxone, and cefuroxime through acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 5. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of celecoxib via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 6. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of chlorothiazide and chlorthalidone through acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 7. Choline magnesium trisalicylate decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing renal clearance. Rose hips, in turn, increase the levels or effects of choline magnesium trisalicylate by acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance and by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 8. Rose hips enhance the GI absorption of chromium, increasing its levels. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 9. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 10. Conjugated estrogens (oral and vaginal forms) decrease the levels of rose hips by increasing their elimination. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 11. Rose hips decrease the levels of copper by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 12. Rose hips decrease the levels of cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 13. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of cyclopenthiazide via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 14. Ascorbic acid (a component of rose hips) increases the availability of iron for chelation with deferoxamine. This interaction should be avoided in patients with cardiac failure undergoing deferoxamine therapy. Clinical cardiac monitoring is recommended. Deferoxamine decreases the levels of rose hips by inhibiting their GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Rose hips decrease the levels of demeclocycline by inhibiting its GI absorption. Demeclocycline decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing their elimination. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 16. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 17. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of diclofenac via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 18. Didanosine decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 19. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of diflunisal via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. Diflunisal decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing renal clearance. Rose hips also increase diflunisal levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 20. Rose hips decrease the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting its GI absorption. Doxycycline decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing their elimination. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is serious, and alternative therapies are recommended. 21. Rose hips decrease the levels of eltrombopag by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The combination is contraindicated, and administration should be separated by at least 4 hours. 22. Enalapril and rose hips may interact through an unknown mechanism, potentially causing gastrointestinal symptoms and hypotension. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 24. Estradiol, synthetic conjugated estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate decrease the levels of rose hips by increasing their elimination. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 25. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of etodolac via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 26. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 27. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of fenbufen, fenoprofen, flurbiprofen, and ganciclovir via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 28. Rose hips decrease the levels of fleroxacin, gemifloxacin, and moxifloxacin by inhibiting their GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies are recommended. 29. Gymnema decreases the levels of rose hips by inhibiting their GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 30. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of hydrochlorothiazide, indapamide, indomethacin, ketoprofen, ketorolac (oral and intranasal forms), lornoxicam, meclofenamate, mefenamic acid, meloxicam, and mesalamine via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 31. Mesalamine decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing renal clearance. Rose hips also increase mesalamine levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 32. Mestranol decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing their elimination. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 33. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of methotrexate, methyclothiazide, and metolazone via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 34. Rose hips decrease the levels of methyldopa by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 35. Rose hips decrease the levels of minocycline by inhibiting its GI absorption. Minocycline decreases the levels of rose hips by increasing their elimination. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is serious, and alternative therapies are recommended. 36. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of mycophenolate via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. However, rose hips also decrease mycophenolate levels by inhibiting its GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative therapies are recommended. 37. Rose hips decrease the levels of levocarnitine through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is minor and unknown. 38. Rose hips decrease the levels of levothyroxine and liothyronine by inhibiting their GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. This summary provides detailed, professional descriptions of the interactions between rose hips and various drugs, as requested.
